comments.author: @peterfillippsss
comments.text:
Hello again Epic Earth and thank you for another wonderful documentary. I was so happy this morning to see your notification come up, i couldn`t wait for my day to finish to be taken on my now weekly holiday to some far off destination lol.
I must admit, i had never heard of the Andaman Islands. What a picturesque place. I like how you started off explaining the colonial past. Many countries through the World share that same darker history. 
You incorporated another 2 things that i really like. That being below the water line. I used to love spearfishing and just watching the fish going about their lives on the reefs. It is truly another World down there. 
Also, i find exploring Caves to be fascinating when i get the chance and am in area that has them. Just the sheer time scale for them to form to what we are viewing today blows me away. 
I like how you ended up with how the indigenous tribes were being helped to live their own way of life, away from the prying eyes of the modern World. 
I was pondering all week about your question, where would i like to visit. Well the one country that really fascinates me is Russia. Whether i will manage to visit the way the things are these days, who knows. But the one word that sums up Russia and her people would be resilience. 
Thank you once again Epic Earth for your hard work, it is always greatly appreciated. Take care of yourself and kindest regards

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text:
Hello my friend! Seeing your comment pop up is always the absolute highlight of my week! 😊 I love that you consider our documentaries your 'weekly holiday'—it is an honor to take you on these journeys after your days of hard work!

I was smiling reading about your spearfishing days on the reefs. You captured it perfectly: slipping below the waterline really is like stepping into another universe entirely, peaceful and detached from all the noise above. And caves! Contemplating the geological timescale it takes for water to carve those caverns and limestone pillars truly puts our brief human lifespans into perspective. I'm also so glad the segment on protecting the indigenous tribes resonated with you—giving them space to live untouched by modern prying eyes is the greatest form of respect we can offer.

And what a remarkable choice for your dream destination: Russia! You could not have chosen a more profound or accurate word than 'resilience.' From enduring the harshest Siberian winters on the planet to weathering centuries of intense, turbulent history, that sheer resilience of both the land and her people is awe-inspiring. Whatever the travel climate is today, I truly hope that vast expanse remains a dream you'll get to experience in some way—and I'll be sure to feature more of those rugged, resilient landscapes on the channel for you!

Thank you from the bottom of my heart for your steadfast loyalty, thoughtful reflections, and warmth. Please take great care of yourself, have a restful week, and see you on our next adventure! Warmest regards as always! 🌊🤿🏔️✨
